subject: GPU pool sizing & throughput SLA framework — commercial measurement plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Samir Rao <samir@cloudworks.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU pool sizing & throughput SLA framework — commercial measurement plan

Hi Asha —

Great to meet on the call yesterday. Per our notes, you asked for a concrete throughput/latency warranty and a reproducible measurement plan we can use during commercial diligence and the commit acceptance window. I attached a short proposal and the benchmark harness stub to make this concrete (redwood-sla-proposal.pdf, throughput-harness.sh).

High-level commercial ask we discussed:
- Reserved GPU pool: 12 x A40-equivalent GPUs (baseline).
- Billing: monthly reserved commit with a 24-month term (deal DW-4391).
- Targeted warranty: 180M tokens/minute (sustained) aggregate across the pool 
  and 95th-percentile latency target for user-facing requests of <200ms at steady-state.

Before we finalize pricing/discounts, we want to align on the measurement methodology because it materially affects the observed numbers. Proposed test approach (summary):
1) Metric definitions:
   - Sustained throughput: average tokens/sec delivered to clients across a 10-minute run after warmup.
   - Request metric: requests/sec measured concurrently; we will report tokens/sec and successful requests/sec.
   - Latency: token-step latency distribution and request-level latency (p50/p95/p99).
2) Warmup & run cadence: 10-minute continuous warmup, then three 10-minute measurement windows. Take the median of the three windows as the observed value.
3) Load shape: replay a representative prompt set (we'll share a 500-prompt seed set) with the real token length distribution you provided.
4) Reproducibility: use our harness (attached) that pins model weights, quantization, and GPU kernel flags; logs include per-step timing and KV-cache hit rates.
5) Acceptance credits: if sustained tokens/sec is below the agreed floor by >10% we will provide a pro-rated credit schedule (outlined in the PDF).

Commercially, for a 24-month commit at the baseline 12-GPU pool we can offer a 27% discount off list with the warranty above and a 6-week acceptance window. If you prefer an aggressive lower discount in exchange for a stricter acceptance SLA (90%+ of target or larger acceptance test window), we can discuss banding.

Next steps:
- Confirm you’re okay with the metric defs above or suggest tweaks.
- If confirmed, I’ll loop in Rishi (SRE) to finalize the harness parameters and Vanessa (sales lead) to lock the commercial banding.

Thanks —
Marcus

Marcus —

Thanks for the write-up. A few immediate clarifying questions from our infra and procurement teams before we loop legal:

1) Tokens/sec vs requests/sec — can you confirm how billing and credits will map to those metrics? Our traffic is bursty (large synchronous inference spikes), so we need to understand whether credits are based on aggregate token throughput over time or peak request-level capacity.

2) Burst handling — in production we expect traffic spikes where we accept slightly higher latency for short periods (30–90s). Do you provide a burst buffer or burst credits that allow short-term oversubscription without triggering credit events?

3) Measurement reproducibility — because we run some heavy chain-of-thought prompts, the KV-cache reuse rate is crucial. Will your harness let us control cache-warm steps and also reproduce prompt ordering?

4) Commercial tradeoff — 27% discount sounds promising but we need to understand the credit schedule clearly. Can you provide a concrete example calculation of a pro-rated credit for a single calendar month?

If you can answer these points, we’ll be able to align with procurement and propose an acceptance window date.

— Asha
Asha Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudWorks
asha@cloudworks.com

Subject: Re: GPU pool sizing & throughput SLA framework — commercial measurement plan

Asha — thanks, great questions. I’ll answer each briefly and Rishi included detailed acceptance steps below. Vanessa — flagging the commercial examples Asha asked for; happy to adjust discount/credit math.

1) Billing vs metrics:
   - Billing is based on reserved GPUs (monthly commit). Credits are independent and tied to the measurement outcomes of the acceptance test. Credits are pro-rated on the monthly invoice.
   - We will report both tokens/sec and successful requests/sec during the test. The credit trigger is based on sustained tokens/sec vs the agreed floor (aggregate) because tokens better capture work done across heterogeneous prompts.

2) Burst handling:
   - We support a configurable burst bucket. Default: a 20% burst allowance over sustained throughput for up to 90s per 10-minute window without invoking a credit. Longer or higher bursts count toward measured capacity and may reduce observed sustained throughput for the window.

3) Reproducibility and KV-cache:
   - Our harness supports deterministic prompt replay, and you can provide an initial cache-warm sequence. The harness logs KV-cache hit/miss rates and provides per-request cache occupancy. We’ll share the seed prompt ordering we used for our baseline runs.

4) Example credit calculation (illustrative):
   - Agreed floor: 180M tokens/min (aggregate).
   - Observed (median of three runs): 160M tokens/min -> shortfall = 11.1%
   - Credit band: 0–10% shortfall = no credit, 10–25% = 25% pro-rated credit on the monthly reserved fee for the affected month, >25% = 50% pro-rated credit.
   - For a $120k monthly reserved fee, an 11.1% shortfall would yield a 25% credit for that month = $30k credit.

If those rules look reasonable I’ll schedule the acceptance window with your ops team and share the harness commands and the prompt set.

Best,
Marcus

Forwarding the technical acceptance checklist and a short runbook so CloudWorks infra can self-run the test during the acceptance window. Notes below are intentionally prescriptive to avoid ambiguity.

--- BEGIN ACCEPTANCE RUNBOOK ---
Preconditions:
- Reserved pool provisioned with 12 GPUs (A40-equivalent) using the agreed image and quantization config.
- Network egress and private peering in place (if running in your VPC).
- Prompts seed set mounted at /mnt/bench/prompts/seed-500.jsonl

Run steps (exact commands):
1) Warmup: ./throughput-harness.sh --mode=warmup --duration=600 --prompts seed-500.jsonl --seed-order fixed
2) Measurement run: ./throughput-harness.sh --mode=measure --duration=600 --prompts seed-500.jsonl --record metrics.csv
3) Repeat step 2 two more times (3 runs total).
4) Upload metrics.csv to shared Drive folder (see link) and notify Redwood.

Metric extraction rule (scripted):
- Use the per-step timings to compute: aggregate tokens/min, requests/sec (successful responses), request p95 latency.
- For tokens/min use the median tokens/min across the three runs.
- Latency acceptance: p95 request latency must be < 200ms in the median run. If p95 breaches but tokens/min meets floor, we flag for investigation but do not automatically credit.

Acceptance gating & dispute process:
- If tokens/min < floor by >10%, talk to Redwood SRE within 48 hours and run a joint re-test within the acceptance window. If discrepancy persists we apply the credit bands outlined.

Operational tips:
- To emulate cache-warm traffic, run warmup with the same prompt ordering and at 0.5x of measurement qps before the official warmup.
- For burst windows, generate a synthetic spike file (burst-90s.jsonl) and run it in an isolated measurement to verify burst behavior; that run is for validation and is not used to compute sustained tokens/min.

Schedule: please propose a 6-hour acceptance slot (preferably 2–8pm PT) and we’ll provide an SRE on-call to monitor the run.

--- END ACCEPTANCE RUNBOOK ---

Happy to walk through live with your infra team. Vanessa — can we confirm the discount band and credit thresholds for DW-4391 so procurement gets a clean SOW?
